Subject: Recap & next steps: Greenfield Health private/VPC connectivity and air-gap requirements

Hi Sara / Tim —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we’re all aligned. Please correct me where I’ve misunderstood.

Key pain points you called out:
- Production workloads must not call out to the public internet from the PHI VPC (air-gapped runbook for model serving).
- Data residency requirement: PHI storage and logs must remain in your AWS account / us-east-1 and not be replicated to external regions.
- Customer-managed key material (KMS/HSM) for model keys and audit exports.
- Network ops constraint: no incoming connections to prod subnet from Internet; any third-party must terminate via your DMZ/bastion or approved Transit Gateway attachments.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Proof of concept running Redwood Private in a customer VPC with a restricted egress pattern (VPC peering/PrivateLink or Transit Gateway).
2) Provide a connectivity playbook that lists required firewall rules, allowed IP ranges, DNS flows, and port/protocol needs so your network team can pre-approve.
3) Confirm KMS integration options and audit log retention policy that meets your compliance bar.

Immediate asks from us to you:
- Share your current network diagram for the PHI VPC (subnets, NAT, TGW, bastion stacks).
- Confirm the outbound egress policy (completely blocked vs. allowed to specific private endpoints).
- Provide procurement contact for template contract and SOC2 evidence request.

What we’ll deliver by next week (target 2026-05-18):
- Draft "connectivity playbook" (PDF) with minimal firewall rules and a recommended deployment pattern (VPC peering vs. on-prem agent).
- Short KMS integration note and list of required audit logs/events.
- A calendar invite for an architecture deep-dive with our infra engineers (proposed: 2026-05-18 10:00 AM PDT).

Attachments: call notes (summary), placeholder for playbook to follow.

If that looks right, I’ll send the calendar invite and attach the first-draft playbook.

Thanks —
Hannah

Hannah —

Thanks for the thorough recap. That matches our notes. A few clarifications and a couple of docs attached:

Clarifications:
- Our prod VPC is fully restricted from the public internet. Any third-party traffic must traverse the DMZ and be inspected by our NGFW. We can allow traffic to a static set of private IPs via TGW if needed.
- We cannot accept inbound connections into the PHI subnets; work must originate from our side or terminate at an approved DMZ endpoint.
- KMS: we use CloudHSM-backed CMKs in our account; any integration must be able to call our KMS endpoints from the Redwood control plane that runs in-hosted mode or be supported entirely within our VPC.

Attachments included: greenfield_network_diagram.pdf, soc2_scope.xlsx
Procurement contact: procurement@greenfieldhealth.com (cc’d on this thread).

Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & next steps: Greenfield Health private/VPC connectivity and air-gap requirements

Quick notes after a scan of the diagram and Sara’s notes:
- Recommendation: start with a in-customer-VPC deployment using Transit Gateway attachments + PrivateLink for control-plane communication. This avoids shipping hardware and keeps logs in their account.
- Constraint: since PHI subnets cannot accept inbound, our control plane must either:
  1) run connectors in their VPC that initiate egress to an approved private endpoint (preferred), or
  2) rely on a maintenance window where their bastion pulls artifacts (more operational friction).
- KMS: CloudHSM-backed CMKs are fine; we need an IAM role in their account and either an endpoint reachable from the connector subnets or a short-lived proxy in their DMZ.
- DNS: will need conditional forwarding for model-serving hostnames if we put resolver in prod.

Questions for Sara/team:
- Can the connector subnets initiate TLS to a private endpoint we provide (PrivateLink) or to a small set of static egress IPs through the TGW?
- Any constraints on using Transit Gateway vs. VPC peering?

I’ll assemble the IP/port table and a diagram variant (PrivateLink + connector) by tomorrow.

-Vivek
